roadmap.title: Career Launchpad: Comprehensive Resume, Portfolio, and Interview Mastery
roadmap.description: A 3-month intensive journey designed to transform a beginner into a job-ready candidate by mastering the art of self-presentation, digital presence, and high-stakes interview performance.

topics.title: Resume Architecture and ATS Optimization
topics.explanation: Understanding the structure of professional resumes and how to pass automated screening systems.
notes: Reverse-Chronological Format: Listing experiences from most recent to oldest is the industry standard for readability.
ATS (Applicant Tracking Systems): Software used by recruiters to filter resumes based on keywords and formatting.
Quantifying Achievements: Using metrics (e.g., 'Increased sales by 20%') instead of just listing duties.
Contact Information & Professional Summary: Crafting a 3-sentence hook that defines your value proposition immediately.
Formatting Rules: Avoiding complex graphics, tables, or columns that can confuse ATS parsers.
exercises: Convert a functional resume into a reverse-chronological format.
Audit a job description and extract 10 key skills to include in a target resume.

quizzes.question: In a reverse-chronological resume, which job should be listed first?
options: Your most recent or current job
The job most relevant to the new role
The job you stayed at the longest
quizzes.answer: Your most recent or current job

quizzes.question: Why should you avoid using tables or images in an ATS-friendly resume?
options: They take up too much space
ATS software may fail to parse the text inside them
They make the file size too large
quizzes.answer: ATS software may fail to parse the text inside them

topics.title: Personal Branding and LinkedIn Strategy
topics.explanation: Establishing a professional digital footprint that complements your resume.
notes: LinkedIn Headline: Moving beyond 'Student at University' to a skill-based professional headline.
The 'About' Section: Writing a narrative-driven summary that highlights career goals and personality.
Skill Endorsements and Recommendations: Building social proof through peer and mentor validation.
Engagement Strategy: How to share industry content and comment on posts to increase profile visibility.
Professional Photography: The impact of a high-quality, approachable headshot on recruiter outreach.
exercises: Write a 150-word LinkedIn 'About' section in the first person.
Identify 5 industry leaders and engage with their latest posts meaningfully.

quizzes.question: Which part of a LinkedIn profile is most important for appearing in recruiter searches?
What is the recommended tone for a LinkedIn 'About' section?

project.title: The Master Application Suite
project.description: Create a comprehensive 'Master Resume' containing all possible experiences, a 'Targeted Resume' for a specific job description, and a fully optimized LinkedIn profile including a custom banner and summary.

topics.title: Portfolio Curation and Storytelling
topics.explanation: Selecting and presenting work samples that prove your technical and soft skills.
notes: Selection Criteria: Choosing 3-5 projects that demonstrate a range of capabilities.
Case Study Format: Explaining the Problem, the Process, and the Result for each project.
Visual Presentation: Using clean layouts, screenshots, or code snippets to make work accessible.
Platform Selection: Choosing between GitHub (Dev), Behance (Design), or a personal website (General).
Proof of Impact: Including testimonials or data that validates the success of your projects.
exercises: Draft a 'Problem-Solution-Impact' outline for your strongest project.
Select a hosting platform and set up the basic navigation structure.

quizzes.question: What is the most important element of a portfolio project description?
options: The narrative of the process and the final result
quizzes.answer: The narrative of the process and the final result

quizzes.question: How many projects are typically recommended for a beginner's portfolio?

topics.title: The STAR Method and Behavioral Interviewing
topics.explanation: Mastering the structured technique for answering 'Tell me about a time when...' questions.
notes: Situation: Setting the scene and providing context for your story.
Task: Explaining the specific challenge or goal you were facing.
Action: Describing the exact steps YOU took to address the situation (using 'I' not 'we').
Result: Highlighting the positive outcome, quantified if possible.
Common Pitfalls: Spending too much time on the Situation and not enough on the Action.
exercises: Prepare STAR responses for the top 5 behavioral questions (e.g., Conflict, Failure, Leadership).
Record yourself answering one question and time the 'Action' portion to ensure it is at least 60% of the response.

quizzes.question: In the STAR method, what does the 'R' stand for?
Which part of the STAR method should receive the most detail and time?

project.title: Digital Portfolio Launch
project.description: Develop a live digital portfolio containing at least three detailed case studies. Each case study must follow the STAR framework and include visual evidence of the work performed.

topics.title: Interview Psychology and Body Language
topics.explanation: Managing nerves and project confidence through non-verbal communication and mindset.
notes: First Impressions: The importance of the 'Entrance' and the first 30 seconds of interaction.
Active Listening: Using nodding and clarifying questions to show engagement.
Virtual Interview Etiquette: Lighting, background, and maintaining eye contact with the camera.
Handling Stress: Techniques for pausing and thinking before answering difficult questions.
Confidence vs. Arrogance: Striking the right balance when discussing achievements.
exercises: Conduct a 'Power Pose' session before a practice call to boost confidence.
Practice an 'Eye Contact' drill by looking at the webcam lens specifically while speaking.

quizzes.question: Where should you look during a virtual interview to simulate eye contact?
options: At the interviewer's face on the screen
Directly into the computer's camera lens
quizzes.answer: Directly into the computer's camera lens

quizzes.question: If you are asked a question you don't know the answer to, what is the best approach?
options: Stay silent until they move on
Acknowledge the question, explain your thought process, and relate it to what you do know
Say 'I don't know' and stop talking
quizzes.answer: Acknowledge the question, explain your thought process, and relate it to what you do know

topics.title: Mock Interview Mastery and Negotiation
topics.explanation: Simulating the full interview experience and learning to handle job offers.
notes: The 'Elevator Pitch': Perfecting the 'Tell me about yourself' response in under 90 seconds.
Asking Reverse Questions: Preparing high-level questions for the interviewer to show interest.
Salary Negotiation: Researching market rates and deferring salary talk until an offer is made.
Post-Interview Follow-up: Writing a thank-you email that reinforces your value.
Feedback Loops: How to ask for and implement feedback from unsuccessful interviews.
exercises: Record a 20-minute mock interview with a peer or using an AI tool.
Draft a template for a post-interview thank-you note that references a specific conversation point.

quizzes.question: What is the primary purpose of asking the interviewer questions at the end?
options: To prove you did research and are genuinely interested in the company culture
To make the interview last longer
To find out how much you will get paid
quizzes.answer: To prove you did research and are genuinely interested in the company culture

quizzes.question: When is the best time to negotiate your salary?
options: After you have received a formal job offer
quizzes.answer: After you have received a formal job offer

project.title: The Final Simulation
project.description: Complete a 3nd-party mock interview (via platform or mentor). Review the recording, write a 500-word self-critique identifying three areas of improvement, and update your 'Interview Cheat Sheet' with refined STAR stories.
